status: proposed scope extension, not adopted or implemented; existing accepted build-generation choices remain unchanged
user_question: Are model/field traits the only inline Given prompt use-case? What about prompted policy, unique, invariant, lock and new local Given vocabulary?

current_answer.implemented: Current compiler has closed Given declarations and no accepted generation-engine implementation or general custom-keyword registration.
current_answer.accepted: Named/inline trait supports model/field composition, including supported model invariants/hooks; it excludes first-class prompted policy/unique/lock targets and generated policy grants.

recommended_outcome: Expand Given generation to source-owned declarations and computations beyond model/field traits. Support inline prompts behind explicit canonical rule headers and named reusable local rules. Preserve the saved selected-unit lifecycle, zero-AI ordinary builds and canonical enforcement.

proposed_targets.contract: Explicit read principals and field grants remain in authored policy headers; generate the additional row/eligibility predicate. No implied grant from a domain adjective.
proposed_targets.example: policy Claim read=reviewer where=$"Only claims at a location this reviewer is assigned to."

proposed_targets.contract: Pure rule over proposed final owner state with explicit dependency/read contracts; relevant changes recheck dependent rows. No effects or silent query truncation.
proposed_targets.example: invariant Booking: $"Active bookings for the same desk must not overlap."

proposed_targets.contract: Authored field selectors; generated condition evaluates on canonical pre-state and preserves sealing-transition behavior and deletion rules.
proposed_targets.example: lock Invoice fields=number,total,currency when=$"Once this invoice has been issued."

proposed_targets.contract: Saved checked key/scope/normalization/null/conditional semantics, canonical owner-level atomic enforcement for every write. An ordinary JS search before writing is insufficient.
proposed_targets.example: unique Customer $"The normalized company registration reference must be unique within this operator."

proposed_targets.contract: Explicit owning field or typed function signature and exact representations; supported pure runtime role and declaration dependencies. Existing built-in rules stay directly expressible without AI.
proposed_targets.example: derive Deal.priority:int=$"Return a deterministic priority from its declared stage and next-action time; do not use wall-clock or external data."

proposed_targets.contract: A typed compatible target and visible checked output contributions; reuse one definition unit without an AI call at each application. May compose existing invariants, keys, locks, fields and computations; built-in names and enforcement cannot be redefined.
proposed_targets.example:
rule append_only $"Make the target record append-only using canonical locks; preserve its declared reads and create authority."
append_only Movement

syntax_status: Proposed examples now use the human-suggested $"..." generation-prompt literal, documented in design/proposals/build-generation/prompt-literal.json. This distinguishes generation intent from ordinary strings. Marker, rule spelling, signatures and target scope remain proposals, not accepted grammar; a broadened trait carrier remains an alternative.

concrete_draft_examples.concept: issued invoice number exclusivity and immutable financial snapshot
immutable movements, source exclusivity and dependency-aware nonnegative location balances
queue-scoped staff visibility and sealed submitted replies

integration_boundary: Generate ordinary checked Can contributions where they express the rule; generated workerd JS computations/predicates require explicit typed phase/read/dependency contracts and canonical wrappers. The compiler must expose exact grants/keys/fields/rules and normal migration effects. A genuinely unsupported runtime mechanism remains a diagnosed capability gap, not a successful AI extension.
open_decisions: Whether to extend trait to declaration targets or add prompt-bearing built-in targets and a rule carrier; exact syntax/signatures/local invocation and target/selector arguments.

Explicit generated-JS rule inputs, phase, bounded authority reads and dependency tracking/revalidation contracts; representation of uniqueness scope/key/null/normalization, and supported pure derive role.
Accepted scope change to BGEN and BGI before implementation; these new targets are not silently covered by the old all-four-category completion criterion.

jev_advice.disagreement_investigation: Carrier agreement is weak and third prefers open (.45 versus .41). Source inspection confirms the concrete unresolved target/signature, prompt-versus-literal, uniqueness and JS dependency/phase contracts listed above. Keep examples proposed instead of settling a cosmetic keyword or treating semantic agreement as carrier adoption. No extra model call is required to restate this missing contract.
jev_advice.interpretation: Advice supports a canonical enforcement boundary; neither grammar adoption, implementation correctness nor permission approval follows from probabilities.
